svg.text: KaarigarAI — Screen Wireframes
Six screens · low-fidelity, deliberately · the whole product claim is an interface for someone who cannot read, so it has to be drawn
Grey bars = text the artisan is NOT expected to read.
Every grey bar has a speaker button beside it.
Minimum touch target drawn at 64 px.

g.text: Numeric keypad next — digits, no letters

svg.text: Each tile speaks its own name when touched.
No language list is read. Nothing on this screen must be
understood in writing to get past it — the script glyph is
recognition, not reading. Language stays changeable here later.
One button that cannot be mistaken for anything else.
Framing brackets replace the instruction "centre the product".
Retake prompts are spoken, not written. The green strip means
saved-and-queued — capture never depends on a network.

g.text: English + Hindi · read aloud, never silently published
Noisy recording: it asks again, never guesses.

svg.text: Confirmation is the whole design, in one screen.
The listing text exists but is never required reading — she
presses play and hears it. Two outcomes only: it's right, or
say it again. No editing, no keyboard, nothing to type.

g.text: 4 · WHAT IT IS WORTH, AND WHY
Bar length = how much each raised the price. Tap to hear.

svg.text: SHAP as three bars, not a table.
A band, never a single false-precision number. The floor is
visible and explained in the two words that matter — material
and labour — and it warns without seizing her decision.

g.text: Fixed fields — nothing to translate to act on it
price. You were not shown them.

svg.text: Two buttons. A number she can read. Nothing else.
Offers carry fixed fields — price, quantity, date — so no
translation is needed to act. The shield line is the lowball
protection made visible: she sees that it worked, not the abuse.

text.font-family: Noto Sans Devanagari, Noto Sans Bengali, Noto Sans Tamil, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

g.text: Offers below the asking price are declined
Permanent URL — the printed stall QR resolves here

svg.text: The only screen where reading is assumed.
Buyers are boutique owners, exporters and procurement staff —
so this side is ordinary and plain on purpose. Two sides in one
demo is what most submissions never show.
Wireframes, not visual design: layout, hierarchy and touch targets are the decisions being made here — colour, type and iconography are not final.
Every screen obeys three rules: nothing essential exists only as text · every text block has a speaker beside it · no screen offers more than two real choices.
